content: Turner Memorial Hospital is a healthcare facility located in Keith, Morayshire, Scotland, and operates under the United Kingdom's National Health Service (NHS). It is managed by the NHS Grampian region. The hospital functions as a community hospital with a capacity of 22 beds, offering services such as General Practitioner (GP) acute care, palliative care, rehabilitation, and patient assessment. Additionally, it houses a 24-hour minor injury unit. The hospital's origins trace back to a meeting held on April 28, 1877, convened by Mr. William Longmore to discuss the establishment of a cottage hospital for the parish of Keith. By January 1879, the committee had successfully raised £2,185 and decided to commence construction of the hospital, which was named The Turner Memorial Hospital in honor of the late Dr. Robert Turner. Since its initial opening in 1880, the hospital has undergone numerous changes and expansions. Significant milestones include the addition of the two Kynoch Wards in 1893, as well as major extensions and renovations completed in 1926 and 1992.
